conviction_note: Scaled number is (2*0.48-1)*26 = -1.04: the stock has doubled since the last print ($24.58 pre-print close to $49.50, at its 52-week high, above every dated sell-side target), puts are bid (+12.7 vol pts skew) and insiders sold into October, against a reported quarter that has beaten the top of its guide twice running and new publishers (Uber, 7-Eleven, Giant Eagle) whose first contribution and the promised 2027 commentary are the real swing; the findings sum to about +0.2 because the operating evidence leans mildly positive while positioning leans negative, and the sign of the reaction rests on the Q4/2027 outlook that no source can see in advance, so p_up sits near 50 while abs_move stays at the name's own scale (median 28.5%, implied 23%).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue guide $86-90M (midpoint $88M), adjusted EBITDA guide $12-14M, from the company's Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026051867/earningsrelease63026.htm (2026-08-03). Street revenue consensus $88.6M per Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IBTA/earnings-forecasts (single source; earlier $85.86M per Barchart at the time of the guide, so consensus has drifted above the guide midpoint). EPS consensus disputed ($0.38 Benzinga vs $0.13 EarningsWhispers) and not used. The price, however, trades far above anything the quarter bar implies: the effective bar is the Q4 guide and 2027 commentary management said it would give after the back half.
positioning_check: Short interest (Equibles, FINRA settlement): 3,203,623 shares 2026-09-30 (13.8% of 23.17M Class A outstanding, 15.5 days to cover) falling to 2,765,604 on 2026-10-15 (11.9%, 9.4 days to cover); Equibles model estimate for 2026-10-30 ~2.65M, not official. https://equibles.com/stocks/ibta/shortinterest. Shorts have been covering into the run, so part of the 20d +19.7% is covering; residual short is still ~12% of Class A shares, a moderate squeeze mechanism if the outlook is good. Options: 25d skew +12.69 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.74, total OI only 151 contracts and ATM spread 27% of mid, so the chain is thin. Event-implied move 23.05%. Stock at 0% from 52w high, +157% from the low. Insiders: CEO Bryan Leach sold under 10b5-1 on 2026-10-21 at $48.43-$50.04; nine Form 144s filed 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-30 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001538379.json).

findings.finding: Q3 should land at or above the top half of the $86-90M revenue guide: Ibotta beat the top end of both revenue and EBITDA guidance in Q2 ($88.9M revenue vs a guide topped below that; consensus $84.9M), third-party publisher redemption revenue grew 27% to $61.5M with redeemers +24%, and the Q3 guide already embeds the Walmart deal-day pull-forward into June that management quantified at 2-3 points of Q2 growth; the street at $88.6M sits slightly above the $88M midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (beat top of guide, return to growth) +51.9%; Q1 2026 -0.6%; Q4 2025 +28.5%; Q3 2025 -23.7% and Q2 2025 -30.3% on guide cuts. The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide each time.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide-beat cadence is public; what is not priced into a $88.6M consensus is a print near $90M+. But a modest beat lands inside the guided range the market was told to expect, so it is small; if the market had priced a large beat, consensus would sit at or above the $90M top end rather than $88.6M.
findings.independence: Instacart (a publisher partner) printed ad revenue +23% vs a 15-18% guide for the same quarter, 2026-10-29, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579091/000119312526437014/d24470dex991.htm (filed separately below as its own finding). Q2 call commentary (exit 2026 at mid-single-digit growth) shares the Ibotta-source family: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/10/ibotta-ibta-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

findings.finding: Instacart, an Ibotta Performance Network publisher, reported Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) advertising and other revenue of $331M, +23% y/y and above its own 15-18% guide, on GTV +15%: CPG brands' digital/retail-media spend on grocery platforms was strong in the exact quarter Ibotta reports, after Ibotta last spoke.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of IBTA reacting to a counterparty print in this record; Ibotta's own CPG-budget-driven misses in 2025 drew -23.7% and -30.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty number from four days ago, overshadowed by the DoorDash-Instacart deal headline in the same release; no Ibotta estimate visibly moved (consensus target still ~$35-36). It is a proxy: Instacart ads are sponsored placements, not performance-based offers, and do not mention Ibotta.
findings.independence: proxy only; Ibotta's Q2 call said accounts that declined in 2025 were growing again (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/10/ibotta-ibta-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Kraft Heinz flagged Q3 promotional timing as a headwind (see rejected_candidates), which cuts the other way.

findings.finding: DoorDash agreed on 2026-10-29 to acquire Instacart (~$17B equity value); both are Ibotta publishers (DoorDash multi-year partnership since January 2025, Instacart cited as a redeemer-growth driver), so two of Ibotta's third-party publishers become one counterparty with more bargaining power over Ibotta's take, and analysts will ask about it on the 2026-11-02 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance; partner-concentration news historically moved IBTA on announcement (Uber partnership March 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public but IBTA closed at its high after it, so the market has not marked it as a risk; if it had, IBTA would have sold off on 2026-10-29/30. The deal closes after regulatory approval, so near-term revenue is unaffected; the effect is whatever management says about it on the call.
findings.independence: DoorDash partnership release https://about.doordash.com/en-us/news/doordash-and-ibotta-partner (2025-01-07). Same source document as the Instacart ad-revenue finding, but a different fact (deal vs ad revenue).

findings.finding: Expectations are stretched into the print: IBTA has roughly doubled from the $24.58 pre-Q2 close to $49.50 (52-week high, +19.7% in 20 days, about +83% YTD by early October), above the analyst average target of ~$35-36 (consensus Hold/Reduce), while the CEO and other insiders sold at $48-50 (Form 4 for 2026-10-21; nine Form 144s 2026-10-19 to 10-30) and shorts covered 14% of their position in the first half of October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the run into Q1 2026 (prior print +28.5%) the stock went -0.6% on an in-line quarter; Q3 2025 and Q2 2025, with guides below hopes, -23.7% and -30.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +12.7 vol-point put skew already says downside is paid for, so this finding agrees with the options market and is sized small. What is not visible in the skew is that the remaining short (~12% of Class A, 9.4 days) has been covering, which removes a squeeze buffer; insider sales are 10b5-1 so carry little information.
findings.independence: Short-interest series https://equibles.com/stocks/ibta/shortinterest (2026-10-15 settlement); analyst targets https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/ibotta-nyseibta-shares-gap-up-after-analyst-upgrade-2026-08-04/ (2026-08-04); Leach Form 4 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026067077/wk-form4_1792787300.xml

findings.finding: The print is the first quarter with Uber (native offers launched at the tail end of Q2), Giant Eagle (live July) and potentially 7-Eleven/7NOW/Speedway (11,500+ stores, 'second half of this year', spokesperson said 'fall') contributing, and management said on 2026-08-03 it would give 2027 commentary after seeing back-half results and expected a modest sequential Q4 increase and a mid-single-digit growth exit rate: a guide on these new publishers is the line the stock will trade on, direction uncertain but with more upside levers than the Q3 guide carried.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven every large IBTA move: +51.9% (Q2 2026, return to growth one quarter early, Q3 guide above street), +28.5% (Q4 2025), -46.1% (Q4 2024 guide), -30.3% (Q2 2025), -23.7% (Q3 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Management declined to size 7-Eleven or Uber, so no estimate carries them; but a doubled share price likely already discounts a strong 2027, which is why this is sized at +1 with a very wide band rather than larger. If the market had priced a conservative Q4 guide, the skew would be flatter and the stock would not be at its high.
findings.independence: 7-Eleven launch timing 'fall' per C-Store Dive https://www.cstoredive.com/news/7-eleven-announces-new-promotions-partnership/827087/ (2026-08); Uber partnership https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260325766216/en/Uber-Joins-the-Ibotta-Performance-Network-in-Exclusive-Multi-Year-Partnership (2026-03-25). Whether 7-Eleven offers are live could not be confirmed.

rejected_candidates.detail: Same document and same guide as the reported-quarter finding; the street EBITDA estimate ($11.38M at the time) sat below the $13M midpoint, so it is already in that finding.

baseline_tension: The negative lean (run-up, insider selling, price above every target) agrees with the +12.7 put skew and is therefore largely priced; the operating evidence (two straight guide beats, Instacart ad strength, new publishers) cuts against both, so the net is near zero and the reaction will be set by the Q4/2027 outlook.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning / crowded short): short interest still ~12% of Class A with 9.4 days to cover, so the positioning negative was shrunk from -2.0 to -1.6.

Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 25 to 26 toward the name's own 28.5% median; p_up moved from 47 to 48 because the negative lean agrees with the skew (Rule 3/7), giving -1.04 against -1.5 in the draft.

Rules 1, 2, 5, 6 left the other findings standing: bar is sourced to the company guide; the Instacart item is filed small as a proxy; the reported-quarter finding is kept small because it lands inside the guided range.
